title: Data Enrichment Tools for HubSpot: Lusha, Apollo, Seamless.AI, Cognism, and ZoomInfo — Jon Martin
seoTitle: Data Enrichment Tools for HubSpot (Lusha, Apollo, Seamless)
description: Lusha, Apollo, Seamless.AI, Cognism, and ZoomInfo compared for HubSpot users, plus when HubSpot's own enrichment is enough. Prices checked Nov 23, 2026.
dek: These tools do not all do the same job. Some fill fields on records you already have. Others go find net-new people and direct dials.
Start with the records in HubSpot, then decide whether you need a specialist, and whether you need a price you can see before a sales call.

sections.label: Start with what HubSpot already does

blocks.html: Before you buy a specialist, look at what HubSpot already includes. Per HubSpot, data enrichment is included in all paid plans with HubSpot's Smart CRM, at no additional cost, and data enrichment does not use HubSpot Credits.

In practice, a Super Admin configures enrichment settings, including automatic and continuous enrichment. By default, existing values are kept unless you choose to overwrite them. One caution: smart properties do use HubSpot Credits, so do not fold those into the free-enrichment story.

For firmographics and contact fields on records you already have, this often covers the job at no extra product cost. You buy a specialist when you need net-new people, direct dials, or a large third-party database feeding the CRM.
Pick by the job, not by who has a louder sales team.

items: Already have the records and just need fields filled: HubSpot's included enrichment.
Need self-serve emails and dials with a published price: Lusha.
Want prospecting plus a two-way CRM sync in one tool: Apollo.
Want a large monthly credit allowance and will take a quote: Seamless.AI.
Want sales-led, compliance-first data, pitched at teams selling into EMEA, or standalone CRM enrichment: Cognism.
Want enterprise GTM data with a HubSpot connector: ZoomInfo.

blocks.html: I am not ranking the paid tools by who pays a commission. For a small HubSpot team, the honest order starts with the data you already have.
HubSpot users who searched for a Lusha or Seamless.AI integration, or who are filling gaps in contact and company data. Every option here has to earn its place with a real HubSpot path.
Not for: a generic best-data-tools list with no CRM connection.
Lusha is self-serve, which is why it leads this list for a small team. Prices from lusha.com/pricing:

items: Includes a Free plan with up to 40 credits a month, CRM integrations included.
Starter: $49.90 a month billed monthly, with 400 credits a month, or $37.45 a month billed annually ($449.10 a year).
Professional: $69.90 a month billed monthly, with 600 credits a month, or $52.45 a month billed annually ($629.10 a year).
Premium: $299.95 a month billed annually ($3,599.10 a year).
Credits: 1 credit to reveal an email and 5 credits to reveal a phone number; on monthly plans, unused credits roll over up to twice the plan's limit; annual plans get all credits up front.
Note: teams larger than 5 users go through sales.

blocks.html: HubSpot: Lusha pushes contacts and companies into HubSpot with field mapping, and checks for existing records first so you don't create duplicates, and setup needs admin access on both Lusha and HubSpot. Note that a separate Lusha Signals app on the HubSpot App Marketplace adds a Signals card to each contact record. Two-way compare with Apollo: Apollo vs Lusha.

Apollo finds contacts, enriches them, and runs sequences, while HubSpot keeps the lifecycle. Per apollo.io/apollo-hubspot, Apollo runs a two-way sync of contacts, accounts, and deals, with emails, calls, meetings, tasks, and notes pushed to HubSpot.

items: It is recommended for HubSpot Sales Hub, and it requires an Apollo subscription.
Setup: connecting it takes a HubSpot super admin, and you get 6 hours after enabling to set sync rules before anything syncs.
Apollo's credits are pooled across the team, granted up front each billing cycle, and don't roll over.
Note that all seats on an Apollo account are on the same plan.

blocks.html: Prices from apollo.io/pricing: Basic $65 a month on monthly billing, or $49 per seat per month, billed annually; Professional $99 a month on monthly billing, or $79 per seat per month, billed annually. There is a free plan that stays free with no time limit. More detail: my Apollo write-up.
Set the push rules during that configuration window before anyone imports a list. Loose rules are how a portal gets bloated for a quarter.

Seamless.AI is a contact-data tool. The HubSpot question is what happens when reps click import. Per its HubSpot page, it imports real-time verified emails and phone numbers into HubSpot, and finds look-alike contacts and accounts inside HubSpot. Connecting it means every user who connects needs App Marketplace Access in HubSpot.

Price: the pricing page asks for your details to quote a price; no paid prices are published. There is also a free tier: a Free license gets 50 Universal Credits that don't replenish. Per its help article, the per-license allowances are 250 credits per user per month on a Basic license and 10,000 credits per user per month on a Pro license. A reveal costs 1 credit for an email, 5 for a phone number, or 6 for the full contact. Those are credits, not dollars. Deeper notes: Seamless.AI, and it also shows up in my cold email tools for HubSpot roundup.

Cognism is sales-led. It sells Standard and Pro prospecting packages, each with 5 seats included, and pricing is by quote, with no public price. 1 credit = 1 revealed contact, and no charge for viewing contacts you already revealed. It has a native two-way sync for HubSpot, launched in February 2026; it exports contacts and companies to HubSpot with field mapping and per-field update rules, set up by a Cognism admin. Separately, Cognism lists CRM Enrichment from $12,000 a year; CRM Enrichment can be bought on its own or as an add-on to a Cognism plan, and enriched contacts use credits again only when key details change, like a job move.

ZoomInfo is the enterprise option. It sells flexible packages priced through sales, with no public prices. On HubSpot, it offers Enrich for HubSpot plus the ZoomInfo HubSpot Connector, and adds a Chrome extension that matches what you see on the web to your HubSpot prospects and customers. If you came here comparing it against smaller tools, see my ZoomInfo alternatives for small business. This page is the HubSpot enrichment angle, not that one.

items: Already-have-records versus need-net-new-contacts: start with HubSpot's included enrichment for the first case.
Need a published price: Lusha, then Apollo.
Willing to take a sales call for a larger database: Seamless.AI, Cognism, or ZoomInfo.
Before you connect anything, decide match keys, overwrite-versus-fill-empty, and who can auto-import.

blocks.html: There is no fake winner here that happens to match a commission. The best tool is the one that fits the job you can name.
